security_audit.summary: The static high alerts for screen capture, keyboard input, and environment access are false positives in Playwright testing documentation. Hardcoded URLs, request monitoring, filesystem examples, and Markdown command blocks are instructional or bounded test patterns. One medium semantic issue remains: helper methods interpolate caller-provided values into page.evaluate JavaScript without escaping.

remediation.issue: Unescaped JavaScript interpolation in helper methods
remediation.suggestion: Use Playwright page.evaluate argument passing or JSON serialization instead of f-strings for localStorage keys, values, selectors, and timing values.

remediation.issue: Sensitive test artifacts can be produced during normal use
remediation.suggestion: Document artifact handling for screenshots, videos, traces, downloads, and saved authentication state so users do not commit or share sensitive test data.

semantic_findings.title: Unescaped JavaScript Interpolation in Helper Methods
semantic_findings.description: scripts/playwright_helper.py builds page.evaluate JavaScript strings with key, value, selector, and duration values interpolated directly. If a caller passes untrusted values, the helper could execute unintended JavaScript in the tested page context.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The helper directly embeds caller-supplied strings into JavaScript executed by page.evaluate. This is a real injection risk when helper inputs are not fully trusted, although it is limited to the browser test context.

content.user_title: Automate Web App Tests with Playwright
content.value_statement: Web teams need repeatable checks for browser flows, forms, APIs, and mobile layouts. This skill guides Playwright test creation with examples, fixtures, assertions, and automation patterns.
actual_capabilities: Explains Playwright setup for Python and TypeScript projects.
Provides examples for login, form, e-commerce, mobile, API mocking, and page object tests.
Shows screenshot, video, trace, and visual regression workflows for debugging.
Includes helper scripts for screenshots, waits, storage, network interception, and performance timing.
Documents CI/CD configuration, pytest options, and common troubleshooting guidance.
limitations: It provides guidance and examples, not a managed test runner or hosted browser service.
Example URLs use reserved or placeholder domains and must be replaced before real tests run.
Generated tests still need application-specific selectors, credentials, and assertions.
Screenshots, videos, traces, and saved auth state can contain sensitive data if teams do not handle artifacts carefully.

use_cases.title: Create regression tests for core flows
use_cases.description: Build Playwright tests for login, checkout, forms, and navigation across supported browsers.

use_cases.title: Debug frontend behavior with browser automation
use_cases.description: Use screenshots, traces, network monitoring, and assertions to reproduce and verify UI issues.

use_cases.title: Prepare browser tests for CI pipelines
use_cases.description: Configure Playwright, pytest options, browser projects, retries, traces, and artifact handling for automated runs.

prompt_templates.title: Create a smoke test
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a single page check
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Playwright smoke test for my homepage. Include navigation, a title check, one visible element assertion, and setup notes.

prompt_templates.title: Test a form flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Write Playwright test guidance for a contact form with required fields, invalid email validation, file upload, and success message checks.

prompt_templates.title: Add API and mobile coverage
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced browser behavior and network control
prompt_templates.prompt: Design Playwright tests that mock an API response, verify network calls, and repeat the main flow on a mobile device profile.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a CI regression suite
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced suite design for team automation
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a CI-ready Playwright testing plan for login, checkout, visual checks, retries, traces, browser projects, and artifact retention.

output_examples.input: Create a login flow test for a React app.
output_examples.output: A structured Playwright test plan covering valid login, invalid credentials, redirects, session persistence, selectors, and failure screenshots.

output_examples.input: Improve flaky checkout tests before release.
output: A diagnosis of likely wait and selector problems.
Recommended stable locators and auto-wait assertions.
A revised coverage outline for cart, payment, confirmation, and failure states.

output_examples.input: Add browser tests to CI for a small frontend team.
output_examples.output: A practical rollout plan with browser choices, retry policy, trace collection, screenshot retention, and pipeline setup notes.

best_practices: Replace placeholder URLs, accounts, and selectors before running tests against real systems.
Prefer role selectors, test IDs, and Playwright auto-waiting instead of fragile CSS paths or fixed sleeps.
Treat screenshots, videos, traces, downloads, and saved auth state as sensitive test artifacts.
anti_patterns: Running generated examples unchanged against production systems.
Committing screenshots, downloaded files, traces, or saved authentication state to source control.
Building tests around fixed delays, shared state, or selectors tied to page structure.

faq.question: Does this skill run Playwright tests for me?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance, examples, and helper code that you run in your own development environment.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Which browsers are covered?
faq.answer: The examples cover Chromium, Firefox, WebKit, desktop projects, and mobile device emulation.

faq.question: Are the example URLs ready for my application?
faq.answer: No. They use placeholder domains and must be replaced with your own application URLs.

faq.question: Does it include API mocking guidance?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes Playwright route interception, mocked responses, request monitoring, and offline behavior examples.

faq.question: What security care is needed?
faq.answer: Review artifacts and saved state before sharing them because tests can capture screenshots, videos, cookies, and local files.
